channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Amazon fails to strike out UK class action over alleged “abuse of process”
item.description: Amazon has failed to convince the UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal to dismiss a new abuse of dominance class action against it on the basis that the claim significantly overlaps with another lawsuit.

item.title: Slater leaves the Antitrust Division
item.description: Gail Slater has left her position as chief of the Department of Justice’s antitrust division.

item.title: Australian senator questions “business case” for ex-ante digital markets regime
item.description: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission’s sparse “track record” in launching cases under the country’s existing antitrust laws weakens the agency’s calls for an ex-ante digital markets regime, a senator has said.

item.title: MEP urges EU to scrutinise non-price effects of Netflix/Warner Bros deal
item.description: A prominent EU lawmaker has pressed the European Commission over potential “serious” antitrust concerns stemming from Netflix’s proposed takeover of Warner Bros, warning its possible impact on “European cultural diversity” merits close merger control scrutiny.

item.title: Korea hits sugar cartel with heavy sanctions
item.description: Korea’s Fair Trade Commission has handed down its second-largest cartel sanction, fining the country’s three leading sugar manufacturers €240 million for price fixing.

item.title: “Who’s running the Antitrust Division?”: Slater’s exit raises uncertainty
item.description: The departure of Gail Slater as the Department of Justice’s top antitrust enforcer increases unpredictability amid widespread perception that outcomes can be swayed by political connections, according to several competition lawyers.

item.title: Five-alarm fire: The Tipline for 12 February 2026

item.title: Lazard chair says CEOs must take lead in today's antitrust climate
item.description: Lazard chair Peter Orszag has said the US antitrust landscape now demands direct engagement from chief executives with the Trump Administration, alongside the usual competition analysis.

item.title: Blizzard: California committed to Live Nation trial
item.description: California’s top antitrust cop has signalled the state will continue the fight to break up Live Nation/Ticketmaster even if the US Department of Justice reaches a settlement.

item.title: BREAKING: HSR rule struck down
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission failed to demonstrate that it has the authority to vastly enhance its merger filing requirements under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act, a Texas federal court has ruled, eliminating a reform that Biden-era enforcers said was necessary to detect anticompetitive mergers.
